title: High-Performance, Scalable Geometric Multigrid via Fine-Grain Data Blocking for GPUs
problem: Geometric multigrid solvers on GPUs suffer from high data movement and communication overhead when scaling across multiple GPUs. Performance varies significantly across heterogeneous GPU platforms (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) due to architecture and network differences.
motivation: Geometric multigrid is a critical algorithm for solving large-scale sparse linear systems in HPC applications, and optimizing it for modern GPU supercomputers is essential for scalable scientific computing.
method: Fine-grain data blocking in BrickLib arranges stencil computation data in small blocks matched to access patterns, which reduces the amount of data that must move between memory and processing cores during geometric multigrid V-cycles (multi-resolution solvers). By measuring real-world performance with empirical linear models—mathematical equations that capture memory latency, communication overhead, bandwidth, and throughput—the researchers understand how stencil computations and MPI communication affect overall performance. Testing on NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPU supercomputers shows that this approach maintains consistent performance across different hardware types and scales efficiently when using multiple GPUs.
key_novelty: Fine-grain data blocking—organizing stencil data in small, strategically-arranged chunks—reduces data movement in geometric multigrid V-cycles and improves performance portability across different GPU architectures (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel).
contributions: Achieves 73% peak performance portability metric and 87% weak scaling efficiency to 512 GPUs across three GPU platforms
Fine-grain data blocking technique in BrickLib that reduces data movement in geometric multigrid
Empirical linear model for extracting and comparing GPU latency, overhead, bandwidth, and throughput parameters
Comparative analysis revealing NVIDIA provides lowest overhead and highest throughput per process

metrics.other: 73% peak performance portability, 87% parallel efficiency at 512 GPUs (weak scaling)

limitations: Network bandwidth and latency vary significantly across platforms despite identical Slingshot network infrastructure, indicating platform-specific optimization remains a challenge.
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated multigrid with optimized data blocking
